⚙️ ELI5 Kata · Hamming Numbers (NASM x86-64, 4 kyu)

Hamming numbers use only prime factors 2, 3, 5 (2^i·3^j·5^k): 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 9, 10, 12...
How do we compute all 13,282 64-bit Hamming numbers in 141 bytes of NASM?

https://github.com/8b-is/space-bender/tree/main/katas/4kyu/hamming-numbers

🏭 ELI5 Step 1 (Three Conveyor Belts):

Imagine 3 machines reading already-found Hamming numbers:
• Machine 2 doubles them (`i2`)
• Machine 3 triples them (`i3`)
• Machine 5×5s them (`i5`)
Each step picks `min(x2, x3, x5)` and steps whichever belt(s) tied for smallest!

🚀 ELI5 Step 2 (Zero `mul` Instructions in x86-64):

In NASM we never even call `mul`!
• `×2`: `add r10, r10`
• `×3`: `lea r11, [r11 + r11*2]`
• `×5`: `lea rdi, [rdi + rdi*4]`
• `min`: branchless `cmovb` (unsigned `<`, crucial once values pass 2^63)!

✅ Cached in `.bss` on call #1, so all 13,282 calls take 6 instructions (`hamming(13282) = 18432000000000000000`)!
